correctness.rationale: In K_m□K_n two distinct vertices are distance two exactly when they differ in both coordinates, so exact-distance-two domination of all vertices is total domination of K_m×K_n (never ordinary domination or hop domination). For each row i every possible column j is covered iff there are at least two distinct columns occupied outside i. Inspect the disjoint partition by h=0,1,≥2 strong columns; for h=0, t singleton columns admit m^t−m−t m(m−1) row assignments for t≥3; for h=1 outside labels must occupy at least two rows; for h≥2 automatic. The three generating functions simplify to the displayed symmetric polynomial. For minima, three cells require 3 distinct rows and 3 distinct columns (6C(m,3)C(n,3)); if one side=2, four cells and C(other,2)^2 choices; if min=1 zero polynomial. An independent bitmask enumerator directly tested m,n=(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,3),(3,4), with T_2,3=9z^4+6z^5+z^6. General identity proved by combinatorial partition, finite enumeration only corroborative.

value.rationale: The exact labelled total-domination polynomial and complete minimum-set multiplicity census of the natural two-factor Hamming/rook graph improve previously known minimum cardinalities. All coefficient profiles may be needed in enumerative domination and reliability-style questions, independently of any paper-sized downstream theorem. The distinction from ordinary/hop domination is mathematical, not a renaming.
